title: Derived scalar restriction for ordinary modules has a left adjoint
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings in a universe u and let φ:R → S be a unital ring homomorphism. In a module universe max(u,v), choose unbounded derived categories D(Mod R) and D(Mod S) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The exact functor Res_φ:Mod S → Mod R, which keeps the underlying additive group and restricts the scalar action through φ, induces D(Res_φ):D(Mod S) → D(Mod R). This functor is a right adjoint: there exists a functor L:D(Mod R) → D(Mod S) and an adjunction L ⊣ D(Res_φ). No flatness, boundedness or finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint, following lemma-derived-base-change; derived.tex Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors

proof.text: In the equal ring/module universe construct functorial flat epimorphisms using the free module on the underlying set, with the free-forgetful counit sending the generator at x to x. These supply the source flat-resolution construction. Let F be ordinary extension of scalars R → S, and let B be S restricted to R. Tensor induction shows that Res_φ composed with F is naturally isomorphic to B tensor_R -. An acyclic K-flat complex [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] stays acyclic under this tensor functor, and exact faithful restriction reflects acyclicity. Thus F preserves K-flat quasi-isomorphisms. This entire argument is written in the two private Lean helpers of the module.

Module categories have exact filtered colimits and K-injective resolutions. Apply the already proved source declaration CategoryTheory.Adjunction.derivedAdjunction to the ordinary extension/restriction adjunction, with the preceding flat-resolution and K-flat preservation instances. Exactness identifies the right derived restriction with its levelwise derived functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], using rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. Transporting the adjunction proves the result in the equal universe case. No new existence assumption or postponed proof is used.

For a larger module universe, replace both rings by their universe lifts and use their standard derived localizations. Apply the equal universe result to the lifted ring map. The two lifting ring equivalences induce equivalences on module categories and on the chosen derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], hence right adjoints. The original scalar restriction is naturally isomorphic to the composite of these two equivalences with the lifted restriction: use RingHom.comp_ulift_eq, restrictScalarsComp, mapDerivedCategoryNatIso and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso. Composites of right adjoints are right adjoints; transport along this natural isomorphism.

    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)]

    (restrictScalars.{max u v} φ).mapDerivedCategory.IsRightAdjoint
